claims.claim: [Claude C0] The native installer accepts a specific version number or a release channel (latest or stable), and the channel chosen at install time becomes the auto-update default.

Line 301 reads: 'The native installer accepts either a specific version number or a release channel (`latest` or `stable`). The channel you choose at install time becomes your default for auto-updates.' Installed `claude install --help` (exit 0) reads: 'Install Claude Code native build. Use [target] to specify version (stable, latest, or specific version)', with option --force.

claims.claim: [Claude C1 + GPT O13] autoUpdatesChannel can be set in any settings file, and managed settings can enforce it. Left unset it follows latest. Stable follows a build about one week old that skips releases with major regressions. The setting governs background auto-updates and claude update. The stable/latest toggle dates from 2.1.3.
claims.basis: setup.md (live = capture) lines 229-232: 'latest', the default: receive new features as soon as they're released / 'stable': use a version that is typically about one week old, skipping releases with major regressions. Line 244 covers managed enforcement. settings-reference.md (live = capture, sha256 e7d592dc8ec3baaeaf3156e764f924874e491ffd9af911d5a743edbdafb8452f) lines 5717-5721: 'Choose which release channel background auto-updates and `claude update` follow' and 'Scope: Any file. A grep for 'autoUpdatesChannel' returns 0 hits. A grep for 'release channel' returns only L7374 [2.1.3], L5977 [2.1.92] and L4704 [2.1.153], and none of them changes the default.

slots.correction: The default holds: the precedence stack is as stated, deny-first evaluation is documented, deny rules block in bypassPermissions, and no CHANGELOG line in 2.1.284-2.1.295 changes any of these. Two supporting wordings need fixing. (1) The AN-20 supersedes row says 'hooks that fail to match (now block)', which misreads L594 [2.1.288]. That line is about PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks that were skipped when matching them failed with an error, or when the tool input could not be serialized to JSON; such calls are now blocked. A hook whose matcher simply does not match does not block. (2) 'Nothing overrides a managed key' (settings.md:632) has documented exceptions: for a few security-sensitive keys, a stricter value from a lower level wins over the managed one (settings.md:640). Also qualify C3. Project defaultMode is honored for every value except auto and bypassPermissions only in terminal sessions; VS Code extension sessions don't read project settings for the starting mode (permission-modes.md:110, 298). disableAutoMode is honored from any settings file, not only managed settings (permission-modes.md:84, 325).

family_conflicts.what: introduced_in for the unconfigured auto-mode start default: GPT settings-permissions-O7 records 2.1.285, while Claude C4 records 2.1.284.
family_conflicts.resolution: Not a contradiction. Both families cite the same two lines, and the CHANGELOG supports both per-line versions: L1030 [2.1.284] for interactive terminal and VS Code sessions, and L920 [2.1.285] for -p and Python Agent SDK sessions on third-party providers or with telemetry off. The families only chose different headline versions.

slots.correction: (1) CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR can come only from the shell, user settings or managed settings. Claude Code ignores it in project and local settings env (env-vars.md:425; CHANGELOG L2719 [2.1.251]), so a committed .claude/settings.json cannot switch profiles. The documented multi-account form is a shell alias, e.g. CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/.claude-work claude. (2) forceLoginMethod 'gateway' sends /login to a Claude apps cloud gateway (settings-reference.md:5602, 5608). That is a different provider from the ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL 'customEndpoint' LLM-gateway route (settings-reference.md:5513; llm-gateway.md:44), so it is not the repo's Codex gateway slot. Its support in user settings at 2.1.295 rests on CHANGELOG L13 alone. settings-reference.md:5604 and 5627 (live 04:45Z) still say 'gateway' and forceLoginGatewayUrl are honored only from a managed source. The two sources disagree and the behaviour was not run. This does not carry the default, because the host signs in first-party.

Keep the layered settings and deny-first rules; the bypass decision stays closed. Three corrections apply.
(1) Under the retained bypassPermissions, writes to protected paths such as .claude and .git are auto-approved (permissions.md L90; permission-modes L28, L628). Neither the project's 62 deny rules nor the template's 134 cover the guard set's own files. The only .claude entries are Read(~/.claude/.credentials.json) and Read(**/.claude/.credentials.json). So Claude's file tools can rewrite .claude/settings.json, .claude/settings.local.json, ~/.claude/settings.json, ~/.claude/hooks/** or scripts/hooks/** without a prompt. Edit deny rules would close the file-tool path, since denies block in every mode (permission-modes L30); explicit ask rules would too, since they prompt even in bypass (L38). Bash rewrites stay outside rule coverage, because Bash rules are not a security boundary (permissions.md L251).
(2) The user-template guard wrapper exits 0 when ~/.claude/hooks/secret_path_guard.py is absent, and onFailure:block does not fire on exit 0. The user layer is therefore fail-open on a missing script: latent on this host, where both scripts exist, and live on any host where install_claude_profile.py's guard step did not run. The project hook is fail-closed.
(3) Trust is skipped in every non-interactive run, including piped stdout, not only -p. Those runs use repository hooks, env and apiKeyHelper without trust and silently drop settings files that fail validation, so validate settings and restrict setting sources before trusting headless results.

slots.correction: First, the hardened built-in sandbox bounds only the shell commands Claude runs. Under the host's bypassPermissions, the file and web tools, hooks, MCP servers and status line stay outside it (sandboxing.md L11, L42-43). The docs say to always run --dangerously-skip-permissions sessions inside a container, a VM or the sandbox runtime (sandbox-environments.md L59). It is a real boundary for shell commands, not for the session. Second, allowUnsandboxedCommands false doesn't cover commands the user types at the ! prompt in an ordinary interactive session. That has been so since 2.1.260 (CHANGELOG L2480; sandboxing.md L229-234, L701); the only exceptions are background sessions and Linux sessions with CLAUDE_CODE_SUBPROCESS_ENV_SCRUB. File masking needs 2.1.221 or later, and an extract with no match defaults to warn, leaving the real file readable. deny entries are the plain path.

slots.correction: (a) The order (per-invocation, then frontmatter, then CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, then main) holds only in two conditions. CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE must be unset: with it set, Claude Code ignores frontmatter `model` and Claude cannot pass a model (CHANGELOG L2541 [2.1.257]; sub-agents.md L396-414). And no installed mod may set a model in agent.spawn (sub-agents.md L366). Also, a same-family alias in the parameter or frontmatter resolves to the main conversation's exact model, including [1m] (L368-370). (b) The Agent tool's `effort` parameter applies to non-fork subagents only (sub-agents.md L423). (c) Frontmatter `effort: max` persists because it is in the file (L316). The session-only rule (model-config L622, CHANGELOG L81) applies to /effort and /model picks. Do not set CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL to keep max. It overrides every frontmatter and Agent-tool effort (L316, L423), so every role would run at one level. (d) modelSettings.<model>.effortLevel accepts only low, medium, high or xhigh (settings-reference L1244), so the highest saved per-model fallback is xhigh. A maxEffortLevel cap also exists (L1240, v2.1.267+). (e) If a skill's or command's frontmatter `model` differs from the session model, that turn is a model switch, and the next request reads the whole history with no cache hits (prompt-caching.md L93). (f) The installed --effort help lists only low, medium, high, xhigh and max. Acceptance of `--effort ultracode` comes from the docs only (model-config L634, L644). (g) C9's '$0.20 cache reads' for Sonnet 5.5 matches CHANGELOG L969, but the live pricing.md L29 lists $0.10/MTok cache hits for Sonnet 5.5.

claims.claim: There are two TTL buckets. On a subscription within plan usage, the main conversation gets 1 hour and everything else (subagents, workflows, teammates, forks, compaction, titles) gets 5 minutes. On usage credits, an API key or a cloud provider, both buckets get 5 minutes. Drawing usage credits drops the main conversation to 5 minutes unless a TTL is chosen.

slots.correction:
Name the carrier per session type, and state the precondition that CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL stays unset, because it outranks both frontmatter effort and the Agent effort parameter.
- Coordinator: the launcher's --effort max.
- Non-fork subagents: frontmatter `effort` or the Agent `effort` parameter (v2.1.292+).
- Workflow agents: no per-stage effort option is documented, so the agent definition's frontmatter or the session level applies.
- Teammates: they inherit the lead's level. The definition's `effort` is documented only for in-process teammates, which is the default mode since no teammateMode is set.
- -p workers: they run at the saved modelSettings xhigh unless each launch passes --effort max, because max cannot be saved in settings.
- Codex lanes: governed by the Codex config, not by this default.
- `model: opus` resolves to the main conversation's exact model whenever the main runs an Opus model. A full ID (claude-opus-5-5) is the absolute pin.

claims.claim: A child's model is resolved in this order: the per-invocation parameter, then the definition's `model`, then CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL (a default rather than an override since 2.1.251), then the main model. The same order governs Workflow agents and agent-team teammates.

slots.correction:
1. Teams form only in interactive sessions (agent-teams.md L62), and every worker is a Claude session (agents.md L19). -p workers, SDK runs and Codex lanes are outside this default.
2. 'Used only where workers must message each other' is not enforced by our state. The switch sits in host user settings, so Claude-named subagents become teammates in every interactive session in every project (L60, L230). Host permissions.defaultMode is bypassPermissions, and teammates start in the lead's mode (L290), so unasked teammates would inherit bypass if that mode is in effect.
3. The narrower native route is launch-scoped enablement for the team session only: the shell environment (L50) or --settings, which overrides project and user settings for that session (settings.md L633). Remove the user-settings key or set it to 0 (L431-436). Project settings outrank user settings (settings.md L626), but per-sub-key merging of env was not verified.
4. Choose teams for a Claude lead that plans and supervises (agents.md L44). Plain messaging between sessions you run is covered by cross-session messaging (L46).
5. On Opus 5.5 there is no shared task list without CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1, which the host does not set.

claims.claim: Teams are the only native mechanism with a fixed lead, teammate mailboxes and idle notifications, so they are the choice where workers must message each other. In-process display is the default.

Claude can pass findings with cross-session messaging between sessions you run yourself, including the sessions you dispatch from agent view... Teammates in an agent team message each other directly'. agent-teams.md L484 (lead is fixed) and L486 (split panes need tmux or iTerm2; not supported in VS Code's terminal, Windows Terminal or Ghostty). costs.md L213-216 and L328: about 7x tokens with plan-mode teammates (capture sha256 fdfc7c104df5e97e..., live byte-identical).

claims.claim: A run resumes only within the same session: completed agents return saved results, and a failed agent reruns along with every agent started after it. Backgrounding the session carries the run over; 'Exit and stop tasks' stops it.
claims.basis: workflows.md L378-395 (L391: the exit carry-over is offered only when agent view is on); env-vars.md L245 (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BG_EXIT_HANDOFF); agent-view.md L920 (by default the supervisor starts on demand rather than as an installed service) and L967 (sessions stop if the machine shuts down), capture sha256 2d1d2faddaa1c264..., live byte-identical; CHANGELOG L119 [2.1.295] '(macOS, or Linux without the service installed): running sessions now stop in about a minute unless it is run again'.
claims.correction: WSL2 fit: carry-over depends on the on-demand supervisor. On Linux without an installed service, stopping claude agents stops running sessions within about a minute, and a WSL VM shutdown stops them. None of this has been observed on our workflows (README:1089, per the inventory).

Tasks persist across compactions, and CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID points sessions at a named directory under ~/.claude/tasks/. That works only in sessions that have the Task tools; without them Claude adds nothing to the task list. As a result, Codex lanes and PR review cannot see it.

slots.correction: (1) Register through the template, not ad hoc. The repo manages user scope through adoption/mcp/claude-user.json, where qmd is already http at 2ecce6ec, while the host qmd entry is still stdio. Change the template and re-render, with `claude mcp add --scope user` only as the mechanism, so host-template drift does not grow. (2) The protocol gate for an HTTP service is the v2 runtime's 2026-07-28 negotiation with HTTP servers (mcp.md:322-332; CHANGELOG L1812, 2.1.274), not the 2.1.292 stdio change (L286). (3) Add timeout behaviour to the parity check. Moving a server from stdio to HTTP shortens the default idle abort from 30 min to 5 min when the server sends no response and no progress notification (env-vars.md:329). It also adds a per-request first-byte timer that stdio lacks: the greatest of 60 s, the tool timeout and MCP_TIMEOUT, so 120 s here (mcp.md:418). (4) A shared HTTP service receives no CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR or CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, which mcp.md:117 and :121 and CHANGELOG L4658 set only in a spawned stdio server's environment. serena as launched on this host (--project-from-cwd, per the inventory) therefore falls under the default's own 'stdio stays for per-session state' clause, unless it runs per project with --project, which its installed help offers. (5) -p workers under --strict-mcp-config ignore user-scope registrations, so they need the HTTP entry in their --mcp-config. A per-role --strict-mcp-config set is also a cheaper native way to keep heavy stdio servers out of workers that don't need them. (6) `jcodemunch-mcp serve --help` (rc 0) offers --transport {stdio,sse,streamable-http}, which partly answers open question 4. `semble --help` shows no transport option, and codebase-memory-mcp lists stdio only.
